name: Correlated Cohort Decay Contagion
note: Pools decay evidence across a cohort of economically identical variants instead of monitoring one rule alone. The cohort here is six RSI mean-reversion members (periods 5/9/14/21/34/50) computed on this symbol - the group that average-linkage clustering at rho=0.5 exists to discover, declared in advance because a single-symbol harness has no cross-idea return matrix to cluster. Each member's trailing Sharpe is compared to its OWN pct_win distribution; when the fraction of members below their own mem_pct percentile reaches dead_frac the whole cohort is DEAD, no member may open, and open members are flattened - killing a healthy-looking member is the intended behaviour. Revival needs revive_frac of members above their own median for revive_bars consecutive bars. The published size = base*clip(1-f_c,0.3,1) term is dropped because sizing belongs to the shared harness.
source: Synthesis. The power-pooling rationale is the harvester's; the cohort-level decay premise follows McLean, R.D. & Pontiff, J. (2016), 'Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?', Journal of Finance 71(1):5-32, and Chordia, T., Subrahmanyam, A. & Tong, Q. (2014), 'Have Capital Market Anomalies Attenuated in the Recent Era of High Liquidity and Trading Activity?', Journal of Accounting and Economics 58(1):41-58. Magnitudes from Chen & Zimmermann, FEDS 2018-033.
code:
import math

_PERIODS = (5, 9, 14, 21, 34, 50)
_PCT_STEP = 20          # the percentile table is refreshed every 20 bars


def _rsi(c, p):
    n = len(c)
    out = [None] * n
    if n <= p or p < 2:
        return out
    au = 0.0
    ad = 0.0
    for j in range(1, p + 1):
        d = c[j] - c[j - 1]
        if d > 0.0:
            au += d
        else:
            ad -= d
    au /= p
    ad /= p
    out[p] = 100.0 if ad <= 0.0 else 100.0 - 100.0 / (1.0 + au / ad)
    for j in range(p + 1, n):
        d = c[j] - c[j - 1]
        u = d if d > 0.0 else 0.0
        v = -d if d < 0.0 else 0.0
        au = (au * (p - 1) + u) / p
        ad = (ad * (p - 1) + v) / p
        out[j] = 100.0 if ad <= 0.0 else 100.0 - 100.0 / (1.0 + au / ad)
    return out


def _quantile(sorted_vals, q):
    m = len(sorted_vals)
    if m == 0:
        return None
    k = q * (m - 1)
    lo = int(k)
    hi = lo + 1 if lo + 1 < m else lo
    f = k - lo
    return sorted_vals[lo] * (1.0 - f) + sorted_vals[hi] * f


def family_init(ctx):
    b = ctx.bars
    n = len(b)
    c = [float(x["c"]) for x in b]

    lr = [0.0] * n
    for j in range(1, n):
        if c[j] > 0.0 and c[j - 1] > 0.0:
            lr[j] = math.log(c[j] / c[j - 1])

    lo = float(ctx.p.rsi_lo)
    hi = float(ctx.p.rsi_hi)
    sw = max(10, int(ctx.p.sharpe_win))
    pw = max(60, int(ctx.p.pct_win))
    qq = float(ctx.p.mem_pct) / 100.0
    dead_f = float(ctx.p.dead_frac)
    rev_need = max(1, int(ctx.p.revive_bars))
    rev_f = float(ctx.p.revive_frac)
    base_n = int(ctx.p.base_n)

    members = list(_PERIODS)
    m = len(members)
    rsis = [_rsi(c, p) for p in members]

    # ---- each member's own return stream: the SAME trade at a different
    # lookback, which is exactly what average-linkage clustering at rho=0.5
    # would have grouped into one cohort ----
    sharpe = []
    for k in range(m):
        rk = rsis[k]
        pos = [0] * n
        for j in range(n):
            x = rk[j]
            if x is None:
                continue
            pos[j] = 1 if x < lo else (-1 if x > hi else 0)
        ret = [0.0] * n
        for j in range(1, n):
            ret[j] = pos[j - 1] * lr[j]
        sh = [None] * n
        s1 = 0.0
        s2 = 0.0
        for j in range(1, n):
            s1 += ret[j]
            s2 += ret[j] * ret[j]
            if j - sw >= 1:
                t = j - sw
                s1 -= ret[t]
                s2 -= ret[t] * ret[t]
            cnt = j if j < sw else sw
            if cnt >= sw:
                mu = s1 / cnt
                v = s2 / cnt - mu * mu
                sh[j] = 0.0 if v <= 0.0 else mu / math.sqrt(v)
        sharpe.append(sh)

    # ---- rolling low percentile and median of each member's own Sharpe ----
    thr = [[None] * n for _ in range(m)]
    med = [[None] * n for _ in range(m)]
    for k in range(m):
        sh = sharpe[k]
        ct = None
        cm = None
        for j in range(n):
            if j >= pw and (j % _PCT_STEP) == 0:
                w = [x for x in sh[j - pw:j] if x is not None]
                if len(w) >= 30:
                    w.sort()
                    ct = _quantile(w, qq)
                    cm = _quantile(w, 0.5)
            thr[k][j] = ct
            med[k][j] = cm

    # ---- cohort state machine: contagion, then a slow revival ----
    alive = [1] * n
    dead = False
    run = 0
    for j in range(n):
        nlive = 0
        below = 0
        above = 0
        for k in range(m):
            s = sharpe[k][j]
            t = thr[k][j]
            d = med[k][j]
            if s is None or t is None or d is None:
                continue
            nlive += 1
            if s < t:
                below += 1
            if s > d:
                above += 1
        if nlive >= int(ctx.p.min_cohort):
            f = below / nlive
            g = above / nlive
            if not dead:
                if f >= dead_f:
                    dead = True
                    run = 0
            else:
                run = run + 1 if g >= rev_f else 0
                if run >= rev_need:
                    dead = False
        alive[j] = 0 if dead else 1

    # ---- the traded member, gated by its cohort's health ----
    ref = rsis[members.index(base_n)] if base_n in members else _rsi(c, base_n)
    sig = [0] * n
    for j in range(1, n):
        if not alive[j]:
            continue
        a = ref[j - 1]
        x = ref[j]
        if a is None or x is None:
            continue
        if a >= lo and x < lo:
            sig[j] = 1
        elif a <= hi and x > hi:
            sig[j] = -1
    ctx.sg = ctx.series(sig, "cohort_sig")
    ctx.alive = ctx.series(alive, "cohort_alive")


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.sg[i]
    return s if s else 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    # a cohort declared DEAD flattens every member, including this one
    a = ctx.alive[i]
    return a is not None and not a
